item.title: Taiwan chip giant TSMC says net profit hit record in third quarter
item.description: Taiwanese chip giant TSMC said on Thursday that net profit soared 68.7% to a record high in the third quarter, buoyed by massive global demand for AI hardware.

item.title: Rooms with a view: The highest hotel in France just opened in the Pyrenees
item.description: Featuring 16 double rooms with panoramic views, the Hôtellerie des Laquets is connected to Pic du Midi via a private cable car.

item.title: Thailand: Bangkok protesters decry IMF and World Bank, warn of destructive capitalism
item.description: Hundreds of protesters marched through Bangkok on Thursday, 15 October, in opposition to the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank being held in the Thai capital.

item.title: Can a European Security Council help the EU fight Russia’s hybrid attacks?
item.description: The EU wants a faster political response to sabotage, cyberattacks and drone incursions. Experts say the proposed Security Council could help, but only partly.

item.title: EU leaders enter crunch talks on energy, China and the budget
item.description: Good morning from Brussels, where EU leaders are about to kick off a two-day summit. On their menu today: soaring energy prices, China trade ties and the showdown over the EU’s next long-term budget. Let’s dive in.

item.title: Europe Today: Kallas speaks exclusively to Euronews as crucial EU summit kicks off
item.description: Kaja Kallas, the EU's top diplomat, speaks exclusively to Maria Tadeo as EU leaders arrive in Brussels for a crucial EU summit on spiralling energy prices, an unfinished seven-year budget, and Donald Trump's pressure on Ukraine. We also interview Abu Abughazaleh, the Jordanian Investment Minister.

item.title: Romania says eight people missing after fire on tanker in its territorial Black Sea waters
item.description: The incidents have renewed scrutiny of Europe's ability to protect shipping and critical infrastructure in the Black Sea, more than a year after the EU launched a strategy to strengthen security in the region.

item.title: EU summit: Leaders seek fast solutions to spiralling energy prices
item.description: EU leaders are meeting in Brussels for a packed two-day summit. Energy prices, trade with China and the budget will dominate Thursday's session.

item.title: New four-lane bridge between China and North Korea opens after a decade of delay
item.description: The new bridge's opening comes about a month after North Korea and Russia opened a road bridge as part of their efforts to cement relations.

item.title: ‘They’re not dead yet’: Bleached corals recover in record time after touching healthy clones
item.description: In the lab, bleached corals recovered within just seven weeks of being put in brief contact with healthy corals.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | October 15th, 2026 – Morning
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 15th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Embryo gene editing is getting more precise, but how safe and ethical is the practice? | Euronews Tech Talks
item.description: The use of a precise gene editing technique to edit human embryos has caught the attention of academics and society, yet doubts over its safety and ethics remain.

item.title: ‘Plot twist trips’: Why going off-script is the ‘ultimate travel flex’, according to Booking.com
item.description: In its 2027 predictions report, Booking.com says travellers look set to break out of their comfort zones by taking a trip to do something that’s completely out of character.

item.title: Deepening tech sell-off drags stocks lower as major markets slide
item.description: A deepening tech sell-off drags Asian stocks lower ahead of Europe’s open as South Korean and Japanese markets sink.

item.title: Musk suggests US government behind slowdown in Ukraine's Starshield system
item.description: Elon Musk said any restrictions on Ukraine’s Starshield satellite system are controlled by the US government, not SpaceX. Ukraine’s former defence minister called for the removal of speed limits to strengthen the country’s defence.

item.title: AI in healthcare: from fighting epidemics to family doctors
item.description: A situation report in an hour instead of a day: in Africa's fight against Ebola, AI shows how it can bolster healthcare, in Germany too. But experts warn of opaque systems and unresolved risks.

item.title: Europe’s debt map flips: Belgium borrows like Greece as France pays more than Italy
item.description: Eurozone treasuries are preparing record bond sales for 2027 just as the IMF warns that borrowing costs have hit a two-decade high.

item.title: Indonesia: Bali fuel supply delays spark panic buying and hours-long queues
item.description: Indonesia's resort island of Bali faced long queues at petrol stations on Wednesday, 14 October, as disrupted fuel deliveries left motorists waiting for hours.

item.title: Macron warns student anger is being exploited as France braces for more protests
item.description: With high schools still blocked in several French cities, student unions are urging protests to merge in a fresh nationwide day of action on Saturday 17 October.

item.title: Le Pen lands in Brussels lashing out at the European Commission
item.description: The French far-right leader wants to strip powers from the EU and cap France’s net contribution to the bloc’s budget at €5 billion a year. “Being pro-France does not mean being anti-Europe,” she says.

item.title: Meloni warns Trump's Russian diesel deal is 'very risky' and legitimises Moscow
item.description: Italy's prime minister has attacked the US-Russia diesel deal, warning it weakens sanctions on Moscow. Zelensky thanked her, while the Kremlin hit back.

item.title: Florence’s 'Maricarmen': 94-year-old faces losing her home of 60 years as rent nearly triples
item.description: The elderly widow, almost blind and using a walking frame still does not know about the eviction; her daughter says her story echoes Maricarmen, a symbol of Spain's fight for housing.

item.title: Are Hungary and the EU friends again? The Ring in Budapest
item.description: The Ring visits Budapest to ask whether Prime Minister Péter Magyar has reset Hungary’s ties with the EU. After April’s landslide, Brussels agreed to release €16.4bn in blocked funds, but several issues remain unresolved.

item.title: How Azerbaijan is building its next chapter in tourism
item.description: Florian Sengstschmid, CEO of the Azerbaijan Tourism Board, tells the Travel and Tourism Summit how direct flights, regional investment and a 2030 plan are shaping the country’s future.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | October 14th, 2026 – Evening
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 14th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Hidden for 7,000 years: The twisted skeleton baffling German archaeologists
item.description: Was the Stone Age teenager laid to rest in a twisted pose on purpose, or did the body slip in a sloping grave?

item.title: Thousands of supermarket fridges still exposed after cyberattack
item.description: No group has claimed the attack, and experts warn thousands of similarly exposed devices remain online as a separate incident disrupts Dutch grocer Albert Heijn.

item.title: Mont Blanc rises by almost two metres, now standing at 4,807.47 metres
item.description: An altitude that "is close to the historical value" measured at the end of the 19th century, but still not enough to draw conclusions about the effects of global warming.

item.title: Russia and Ukraine trade blame over Trump’s ‘energy ceasefire’ after deadly Kyiv strike
item.description: A ballistic missile hit a power plant that supplies the Ukrainian capital with heat and electricity, as Moscow said it had downed 900 drones overnight.

item.title: Mont Blanc: new French measurements, summit 'grows' to 4,807m
item.description: New measurements from Saint-Gervais-Mont-Blanc show Western Europe's highest peak at 4,807.47 metres, almost two metres higher than in 2023. Experts say the change is due to the thickness of the snow and ice cap.

item.title: FBI arrest Saudi OpenAI employee for allegedly planting recording device in office
item.description: The ex-OpenAI employee allegedly wrapped a USB device in toilet paper and inserted it into a television located in an "executive conference room".

item.title: Croatia's wartime grievances threaten Montenegro's hopes of joining EU by 2028
item.description: Croatia's list of grievances with Montenegro include missing persons, war crimes, prison camps, property seizures and borders. Podgorica has closed 21 of 33 chapters, but Zagreb is blocking progress unless bilateral issues are resolved.

item.title: Todd Haynes at Lumière Festival: 'It is a time to remember how important it is to protect our freedoms'
item.description: "It is a time to remember how important it is to protect our freedoms, and our ability to speak freely." Euronews Culture sits down with celebrated filmmaker Todd Haynes during this year's Lumière Film Festival.

item.title: Turkish police raid Halk TV in Istanbul, sparking outrage over media freedom
item.description: Police barricades surrounded the headquarters of Halk TV in Istanbul on Wednesday, 14 October, as Turkish authorities raided the independent broadcaster and appointed a trustee to take control of its operations.

item.title: Spanish Foreign Minister tells Euronews 'fundamental rights of people' at stake in snap election
item.description: Albares says upcoming election pits 'progressive majority' against rightwing forces that want to remove fundamental rights. He also discusses Madrid's position ahead of an EU leaders summit on Thursday, advocating to use Russian frozen assets to finance Ukraine

item.title: EU summit: Leaders tackle energy prices, spar over budget and unite on Ukraine
item.description: The two-day summit of EU leaders comes with a packed agenda topped by energy prices, the long-term budget and Russia's war on Ukraine. Hybrid warfare, enlargement and migration will also feature prominently.

item.title: Rutte urges allies to send more air defence to Ukraine
item.description: NATO Secretary General, Mark Rutte said allies need to do more to support Ukraine, especially in air defences. His pleas come amid drastic Russian escalation over the skies in Kyiv.

item.title: Louvre could be forced to close without major overhaul, director warns
item.description: A year after thieves made off with €88 million of crown jewels that have never been found, the new man in charge says leaking pipes and crumbling galleries mean security fixes alone won’t save the Paris landmark.

item.title: Russia’s internet shutdowns push state firms back to landline phones
item.description: State procurement of landline telephones tripled in the first eight months of 2026 as mobile internet outages hit nearly 80% of the country. Rostelecom’s chief urged Russians to keep one at home “like a fire extinguisher".

item.title: Entire Swedish reality show season lost weeks before premiere amid disputed AI claims
item.description: The project could not be restored, wiping out hundreds of days of work, according to Swedish newspaper Aftonbladet.

item.title: Germany: Supporters rally in Hamburg as trial opens over Nord Stream pipeline blasts
item.description: Supporters waving Ukrainian flags gathered outside a court in Hamburg on Wednesday, 14 October, in solidarity with a former Ukrainian army officer accused of involvement in the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline explosions in the Baltic Sea.

item.title: Holidays remain a ‘spending priority’, but ‘cost-conscious’ travel is on the rise, report reveals
item.description: Travellers are planning on booking cheaper accommodation and eating out less while away, rather than giving up holidays completely.

item.title: Major artworks by masters on sale as Monsoon's Peter Simon clears out collection
item.description: Assembled over decades, the art owned by Peter Simon, founder of the Monsoon fashion store, is one of Britain's foremost collections of modern and contemporary art.

item.title: US inflation rises to 3.7% as fuel costs climb ahead of midterms
item.description: Higher petrol prices and airfares pushed US inflation to 3.7% in September, adding pressure on households and the Federal Reserve weeks before the midterm elections.

item.title: Meet the 76-year-old Kazakh traveller on a mission to walk around the world
item.description: Sarsenbay Kotyrashov began travelling on foot in his 70s. After walking across Kazakhstan and through parts of Asia and Europe, he is now preparing to cross the US.

item.title: Exploring Dubrovnik: Lilly’s epic Adriatic adventure of history and thrills
item.description: Dubrovnik welcomes more than a million visitors a year. Join Lilly Douse as she explores its historic Old Town, tries traditional Croatian cooking, and heads out onto the Adriatic Sea.

item.title: Kazakhstan seeks Antwerp-Bruges partnership to boost trade via Middle Corridor
item.description: Kazakhstan is seeking closer cooperation with Belgium on the Middle Corridor, including a potential partnership between the Port of Antwerp-Bruges and the Caspian ports of Aktau and Kuryk, as King Philippe and Queen Mathilde make their first state visit to the country.

item.title: Lufthansa beats Air France-KLM to €1.2bn stake in TAP Air Portugal
item.description: Portugal has chosen Lufthansa to buy a 44.9% stake in TAP, completing the first phase of the airline’s privatisation. The deal still needs regulatory approval.

item.title: World’s oldest shipwreck off Turkey: 4,700-year-old amphorae discovered
item.description: The shipwreck found near Antalya’s Kekova Island, dated to roughly 4,400–4,700 years ago, sheds light on maritime trade in the eastern Mediterranean.

item.title: French journalist Natacha Polony joins growing field of 2027 presidential hopefuls
item.description: She is stepping away from her role as an observer to make herself "useful" to her country, denouncing a France mired in "chaos", amid a debt crisis, "tragic" unrest in secondary schools and a "total lack of prospects."
